title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 16 Jul 2026
summary: On 16 Jul 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, where built-up land covers 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 52.5%. No flag applies to this date, and 100.0% of the circle has data.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: Built-up land returns the brightest echo, 5.55 dB in HH, while the circle as a whole averages -2.31 dB in HH and -13.84 dB in HV. Smooth bare ground is the darkest type, at -22.15 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land, 13.75 km2, has an HV:HH ratio of -16.67 dB, where walls bounce the pulse straight back. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes give HV of -12.88 dB from leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields cover 27.3% at -10.94 dB in HH. Changing fields, 4.8% of the circle, sit at -16.66 dB in HV, which fits fields with little standing crop.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies on this date. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow and look darker. Possible cause of the low HV on changing fields: crops already harvested in early summer; a field visit or the optical photo would check it.
